title: Existence and affine compatibility of relative Proj
statement:
The relative Proj construction in
[def-nagata-relative-proj] exists as a scheme, is independent up to a
unique isomorphism compatible with the chosen affine-chart
identifications, and restricts over every affine open $V\subseteq X$ to
$\operatorname{Proj}(\Gamma(V,\mathcal A))$. These restriction
isomorphisms commute with further restriction and with the structural maps.

proof.text: Use the scheme $X$ and graded algebra $\mathcal A$ of [def-nagata-relative-proj]. Index by all affine opens $U$ of $X$, and put $P_U=\operatorname{Proj}(\Gamma(U,\mathcal A))$, with structure map $p_U$ induced by the base ring map to degree zero. By [lem-nagata-proj-affine-restriction], restriction gives $r^U_V:P_V\to P_U$ for every affine inclusion $V\subseteq U$, over $U$, identifying $P_V$ with $p_U^{-1}(V)$. These are precisely the local pieces and restriction maps required for relative gluing. No intersection of affine opens is assumed affine.

source.place: Tags 01NO, 01NQ: local objects and restriction maps

proof.text: The identity and composition assertions of [lem-nagata-proj-affine-restriction] give $r^U_U=\mathrm{id}$ and $r^U_W=r^U_V\circ r^V_W$ for every triple $W\subseteq V\subseteq U$. Together with the preimage isomorphisms from step 1, these verify every hypothesis of [lem-weil-pbc-relative-glueing-affine-opens]. Apply that node to obtain a scheme $P$, a morphism $\pi:P\to X$, and isomorphisms $i_U:\pi^{-1}(U)\to P_U$ over every affine open $U$, such that $i_U\circ\mathrm{incl}\circ i_V^{-1}=r^U_V$. This proves existence and the asserted affine compatibility, including structural-map compatibility.

For nested affine opens $W\subseteq V\subseteq U$, the two restriction routes under the $i$ identifications are $r^U_W$ and $r^U_V\circ r^V_W$, hence equal by [lem-nagata-proj-affine-restriction]. For arbitrary open restrictions cover the open by affine opens contained in it using [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]; the same equality on those opens proves equality of the restriction morphisms by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing]. Thus restriction isomorphisms commute with iterated restriction, and all maps remain over the base.

Let $(P',\pi',i'_U)$ be any second realization with the specified compatible local identifications over all affine opens. On $\pi^{-1}(U)$ define $a_U=(i'_U)^{-1}\circ i_U$, viewed as a morphism into $P'$. On an overlap use affine opens $W\subseteq U\cap V$. The compatibility equations from step 2 show that both $a_U$ and $a_V$ there are the inclusion into $P'$ composed with $(i'_W)^{-1}\circ i_W$. The opens $\pi^{-1}(W)$ cover the overlap: [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis] gives an affine open $W$ inside $U\cap V$ around every image point. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing] gives a unique $a:P\to P'$ with these restrictions. It is over $X$ since $\pi'\circ a$ and $\pi$ agree on the same cover. Reversing the local comparisons gives $b:P'\to P$; both $ba$ and $ab$ are identities on their respective covers, so that node's uniqueness clause gives $ba=\mathrm{id}$ and $ab=\mathrm{id}$. Any comparison respecting the $i_U$ has local maps $a_U$, and is equal to $a$ by the same uniqueness clause.

source.place: Tag 01LH, uniqueness of the glued compatible local system; morphism-gluing argument

proof.text: Let $(Q,q,j_U)$ be a realization glued from a chosen affine cover $\{U\}$, where $j_U:q^{-1}(U)\to P_U$ are the chosen identifications. On each $q^{-1}(U)$ define $c_U=i_U^{-1}\circ j_U$ as a map to the all-affine realization $P$. For affine $W\subseteq U\cap V$, [lem-nagata-proj-affine-restriction] identifies $q^{-1}(W)$ with $P_W$ through either chart: the overlap equivalence in the chosen gluing is the one induced by $r^U_W$ and $r^V_W$. On this open both $c_U$ and $c_V$ equal the inclusion into $P$ composed with $i_W^{-1}$ and that identification. These opens cover $q^{-1}(U\cap V)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]. Equality on this cover and then [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing] give a unique $c:Q\to P$. Define $d_U=j_U^{-1}\circ i_U$ on $\pi^{-1}(U)$. On $\pi^{-1}(W)$ both overlap restrictions equal the inclusion into $Q$ composed with the inverse of its identification with $P_W$ and $i_W$. They therefore glue to $d:P\to Q$. Locally $d_Uc_U=\mathrm{id}$ and $c_Ud_U=\mathrm{id}$; morphism-gluing uniqueness gives $dc=\mathrm{id}$ and $cd=\mathrm{id}$ globally. The structural maps agree locally, so $c,d$ are over $X$. Any chart-preserving comparison has these local restrictions and is unique. For three covers, their direct and composite comparisons induce the identity on $P_W$ for every affine $W$ contained in a member of each cover; these $W$ cover $X$ by the basis theorem. Morphism-gluing uniqueness makes the comparisons equal. Restricting this equality to any open proves compatibility with further restriction.

blueprint_update.statement:
The relative Proj construction in
[def-nagata-relative-proj] exists as a scheme, is independent up to a
unique isomorphism compatible with the chosen affine-chart
identifications, and restricts over every affine open $V\subseteq X$ to
$\operatorname{Proj}(\Gamma(V,\mathcal A))$. These restriction
isomorphisms commute with further restriction and with the structural maps.

proof.text:
Choose the index set of all affine opens $V\subseteq X$. For each $V$ put
$P_V=\operatorname{Proj}(\Gamma(V,\mathcal A))$. If $W\subseteq V$ is a
principal affine open, quasi-coherence gives the coefficientwise graded
localization

$$
\Gamma(V,\mathcal A)[s^{-1}]\;\xrightarrow{\sim}\;
\Gamma(W,\mathcal A),
$$

and the affine Proj construction gives an isomorphism from $P_W$ onto the
inverse image of $W$ in $P_V$. To cover an arbitrary overlap $V\cap V'$,
index the gluing datum by triples $(V,V',W)$ with $W$ affine and
$W\subseteq V\cap V'$, together with a principal refinement inside $W$.
The associated isomorphism is the map on each standard chart induced by the
displayed localization. Every overlap is covered by such indices, and the
maps are isomorphisms because localization is transitive.

The identity and inverse axioms are the cases $V=V'$ and exchange of the two
affine indices. On a triple overlap all routes send a fraction
$x/s^m$ to its image in the localization at the product of the three
denominators; hence the cocycle axiom is exactly
[lemma-nagata-proj-chart-ring-cocycle]. The datum therefore satisfies
the scheme-gluing axioms, so the Mathlib
construction `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.GlueData.glued` produces a
scheme $P$ and a morphism $P\to X$ (the degree-zero maps agree on every
overlap). Its restriction to $V$ is the specified $P_V$ by the restriction
field of the same gluing construction. A second affine cover produces the
same overlap datum after passing to the common refinement by affine opens;
the uniqueness field of `Scheme.GlueData.glued` gives a unique
isomorphism over $X$ that
respects all the local identifications. (No uniqueness among arbitrary
automorphisms over $X$ is asserted.) The same argument on a third
refinement proves compatibility with further restrictions.
